topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the lecture's scope within the broader cancer course, and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease, contrasting intrinsic stochastic mutation accumulation with environmental risk factors and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how microbial and viral pathogens drive malignancy through mechanisms including chronic inflammation, cell-cycle deregulation, and synergistic immune suppression.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation and chemical carcinogens damage DNA, emphasizing the role of host metabolic activation and DNA adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Microenvironment, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the laboratory and epidemiological methods used to establish carcinogenicity and attribute cancers to specific exposures.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic synthesizes the lecture's core themes and reflects on the practical balance between carcinogenic risks and everyday benefits.
